findings.issue_text: [BUG] The `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` early return executes before the busy-times check, so any slot falling on a day with a date override is declared available without ever being checked against existing bookings. On any day that has a date override, already-booked slots are offered as bookable, producing double bookings for the organizer; the `busy.every(...)` guard at the bottom of checkIfIsAvailable is unreachable for override days.

[BUG] `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is a copy-paste of the `start` line and computes the slot's start-of-day minute instead of the slot end (`slotEndTime`), making `end` always equal to `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` guard can never fire for a slot that starts inside working hours but ends after them (e.g., a 60-minute slot starting at 16:30 against 09:00-17:00 hours is offered, booking past the end of the workday).

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===`, which is a reference comparison and is always false. The intended zero-length-override short-circuit is dead code; a start===end override falls through to the isBefore/isAfter checks where it is treated as a normal (non-degenerate) window instead of the empty window the author assumed.

[BUG] The new working-hours gate compares `slotStartTime.day()` and `slotStartTime.hour()*60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — computed from `time.utc()`, i.e., UTC wall-clock — against `workingHour.startTime/endTime/days`, which are minutes-since-midnight in the schedule's local timezone. For any non-UTC requested timezone the two sides are in different frames: e.g., in timezone -6:00 a 16:00 local slot is 22:00 UTC, so start=1320 > 1020 and the slot is wrongly marked unavailable; conversely early-morning UTC values pass the guard for morning slots in ahead-of-UTC zones, so legitimate schedules return empty or truncated slot lists.

[BUG] `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone)` assumes `override.timeZone` is always a valid IANA string, but `TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional in this same diff (`timeZone?: string`) and is sourced from `availability.timeZone`, a nullable Prisma field. For a user whose availability row has a null/absent timeZone and has a date override, `tz(null)` reaches Intl with an invalid timezone and throws RangeError, turning getSchedule into a 500 for that organizer instead of computing slots.

[BUG] Each flattened date override now carries its own `timeZone` (line 411), but checkIfIsAvailable ignores `date.timeZone` and derives its day-match offset from the single `organizerTimeZone` argument, which the per-user call sites set to one user's availability timezone while `dateOverrides` in availabilityCheckProps contains every host's overrides. In multi-host event types where hosts are in different timezones, one host's overrides are day-matched using another host's offset, so slots on an override day are classified against the wrong calendar day — either offered outside the override window or suppressed on days another host has an override.

[BUG] In the new working-hours rejection block, `end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, making `start` and `end` identical, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` boundary condition never tests the slot's actual end. A slot that starts inside working hours but extends past the working-hours close (e.g. 16:50 start with 30-minute length against hours ending 17:00) is accepted because end (1010) <= endTime (1020); the end-boundary guard the block was added to enforce does not exist, and any future caller relying on it gets silent availability over-extension.

[BUG] When `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` immediately, bypassing the `busy.every(...)` check below, so existing bookings on a date-override day never mark a slot unavailable. On any day that has a date override, a slot falling inside the override window is returned as available without consulting calendar/booking busy times, so a user with an existing accepted booking during their override window is offered that slot again and can be double-booked.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false, making the equal-start/end override branch dead code. Whatever behavior was intended for a zero-length date override (start equal to end) is never exercised: the branch silently never fires, so zero-length overrides fall through to the interval-overlap checks whose behavior for start==end was not the designed one.

[BUG] The new working-hours check compares `slotStartTime` (explicitly `.utc()`) day-of-week and UTC minutes-of-day directly against `workingHours.startTime/endTime` and `workingHour.days` without applying the utcOffset conversion the slot generator applies to the same workingHours structure. For an organizer whose schedule timezone is not UTC (e.g. UTC+6 with 09:00-17:00 local stored as 540-1020), a valid slot at 04:00 UTC (= 10:00 organizer local) has start=240 < 540 and is rejected, removing slots the generator produced as valid; the added test cannot catch this because its fixtures run in UTC where the frames coincide.

[ADVISORY] dateOverrides now carry a per-availability `timeZone` (the very field this PR adds to TimeRange), but checkIfIsAvailable ignores it and interprets every override against the single `organizerTimeZone` parameter. In ROUND_ROBIN/managed-team scheduling where hosts are in different timezones, a host's date override defined for a date in the host's local day resolves to a different calendar day in the organizer timezone and the day-match on line 117 fails, so the override is silently ignored and slots are computed from normal working hours on a day the host blocked.

[ADVISORY] The offset math depends on `override.timeZone`, but packages/types/schedule.d.ts declares `timeZone?: string` as optional, so any producer of date overrides that does not set it gets `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)`, which resolves to the server's local timezone. Existing or third-party callers of getSlots that build overrides without the new field compile fine (the type is optional) and silently compute organizer/invitee offsets against the container's local timezone instead of the override's timezone, producing wrong slot times on any server not running in UTC; the optional type removes the compile-time guard that would force producers to update.

[ADVISORY] The organizer and invitee UTC offsets are both computed at `override.start` and the single `offset` value is then applied to `override.end`, so an override window spanning a DST transition uses the wrong offset for its end. On dates where a DST shift occurs between the override's start and end (or between the override date and the invitee's slot date), the end time is shifted by one hour relative to the intended boundary, excluding or admitting slots along the override's closing edge on exactly the twice-a-year transition dates.

[ADVISORY] The diff's only test addition asserts one happy-path scenario (four slots present for a +6:00 invitee on the override day) and contains no assertion exercising any rejection branch of the new checkIfIsAvailable logic added in this same PR. The genuinely new behavior-bearing logic — slot-outside-override-window rejection on an override day, the working-hours boundary rejection (where the `end` bug and the UTC-frame mismatch above live), and the busy-bypass on override days — ships with zero coverage, so any regression in these branches, including the two bugs already present, passes CI undetected; a regression there re-opens already-booked or out-of-hours slots to booking.

[BUG] The zero-length-override guard compares two dayjs objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which is reference equality on distinct objects and is always false. The intended early-return for a start===end date override never executes, so zero-length overrides fall through to the isBefore/isAfter comparisons and the branch's promised behavior is silently absent; the code ships as a no-op masked by its shape.

[BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed with the identical expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` tests the slot's start minute twice, never the slot's end. A slot that starts inside working hours but whose eventLength extends past `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at the last minute of the day) is accepted as available; bookings can be created for time the user does not work.

[ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable is expanded with a full working-hours enforcement block, which is work outside the PR's stated intent ('date override handling and timezone compatibility') and re-implements, inside the availability predicate, an invariant already enforced by slot generation (working hours gate which slots exist at all). Two parallel hand-maintained implementations of the working-hours rule now must agree; the duplication has already drifted (the broken start/end computation above), and the next change to working-hours semantics has to be made in two places or slot generation and booking-time validation silently diverge — users see bookable slots that the availability check later rejects or vice versa.

[BUG] The new offset math reads `override.timeZone`, which this same diff declares as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts line 5), and only the trpc getSchedule path was updated to populate it — any other producer of dateOverrides leaves it undefined, so `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(undefined)` resolves against the server's local timezone. On the un-updated call paths (the legacy apps/web getSchedule flow that consumes packages/lib getSlots), the organizer offset is taken from the server's host timezone: a deployment not running in UTC shifts every date override by the server offset and returns wrong slot times for date-override days; the fix's guarantee only holds on the one path the diff touched.

[BUG] The router's date-override date matching applies the offset with inverted sign (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` added to the UTC instant), contradicting the convention used in packages/lib/slots.ts in the same diff (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, using the positive organizer offset); for an organizer in UTC+6 the override instant is shifted 6 hours backwards, moving it to the previous calendar day. For a non-UTC organizer, the override's shifted date no longer equals the slot's date, so `dateOverrideExist` stays false and the working-hours fallback (which has no availability on an override day) rejects the slot — date-override days produce no or wrong availability for non-UTC organizers. The added test does not catch this because its organizer timezone resolves to offset 0, making the `* -1` a no-op.

[ADVISORY] The entire new behavior-bearing logic in checkIfIsAvailable — date-override date matching, the dateOverrideExist shortcut, the working-hours fallback, and the organizerTimeZone plumbing — has no test in this diff; the only added test (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts) exercises the separate legacy path through packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots. A regression in the date-override matching or working-hours filter (e.g. the sign or end-minute defects above) ships undetected: every booking-page availability query on the trpc path changes behavior with zero coverage, and the test that was added gives false assurance that 'timezone compatibility' was verified.

[ADVISORY] A linear `userAvailability.find(...)` scan was added inside the per-slot, per-user availability filter on the schedule-generation hot path, executing once per user per slot candidate. Slot computation for event types with many fixed hosts and a wide date range now performs slots × users array scans where the previous code did a direct spread; for large round-robin teams this measurably lengthens every availability request, and the lookup result is loop-invariant per user yet recomputed per slot.

[BUG] In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `end` is computed with the identical expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison tests the slot's START against the working-hour end, never the slot's end. A slot that starts inside working hours but finishes after them (e.g. a 60-minute event starting on the last available minute) passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test and is offered/bookable, producing bookings that extend beyond the host's availability; the check is also semantically dead weight since start and end are the same number.

[BUG] The new `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` early-return reports a slot as available without ever running the `busy.every(...)` booking-overlap check that previously guarded every available verdict. On any day that has a date override, every slot falling inside the override window is returned as available even if the organizer already has a confirmed booking at that time, enabling double-booking on override days; the busy check is now skipped for exactly the slots this PR targets.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false, so the equal-start/end short-circuit is dead code. A zero-length (start === end) date override never short-circuits; control falls through to the boundary checks, which then mark every slot NOT overlapping that instant as unavailable (slots ending before or starting after the instant return true from the find callback → slot rejected) while slots overlapping the zero-length instant bypass the busy check via dateOverrideExist — the exact inverse of any sane interpretation of an empty override.

[BUG] The date-override day match compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` (formatted in the server's LOCAL timezone, since dayjs defaults to local tz) against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where slotStartTime was explicitly forced to UTC via `time.utc()`. On any deployment whose server timezone is not UTC, the override's local-date string and the slot's UTC-date string are computed in two different calendars, so overrides match the wrong day (off by one near midnight boundaries) and override-day slots are silently dropped or wrongly kept; the behavior also becomes server-tz-dependent rather than deterministic.

[ADVISORY] The diff silently repurposes checkIfIsAvailable from a pure busy/seat check into a full bookability check (working hours + date overrides), duplicating availability filtering that getSlots already performs with different math — a second source of truth introduced under a PR titled 'date override handling and timezone compatibility'. Every caller of checkIfIsAvailable gets changed verdicts even on non-override paths, and the two filters can disagree: getSlots shifts override wall-times by (invitee offset − organizer offset) while checkIfIsAvailable re-derives override dates from the organizer tz against UTC slot days, so a slot generated by getSlots can be rejected (or an out-of-window slot admitted) by the second filter; future changes to one path will silently break the other.

[ADVISORY] Three different notions of 'organizer timezone' now feed adjacent checks: the computed `organizerTimeZone` (eventType.timeZone || schedule.timeZone || userAvailability[0].timeZone) is passed to getSlots, while checkIfIsAvailable receives `schedule.timeZone`, `userSchedule.timeZone`, and `userSchedule?.timeZone` (which is undefined when no matching availability is found). A user whose availability row has no timeZone — or the `userSchedule?.timeZone` miss at the third call site — yields undefined, for which checkIfIsAvailable treats the UTC offset as 0 and matches override dates as if the organizer were in UTC; meanwhile getSlots used a possibly different tz, so slot generation and slot filtering disagree about which day an override covers.

[ADVISORY] getSlots now unconditionally calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` while `TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts), so any existing caller of getSlots that passes overrides without a timeZone gets `dayjs.tz(x, undefined)`, which resolves to the server's local timezone. Out-of-tree/internal callers of getSlots whose overrides carry no timeZone silently switch from the old getUTCHours behavior to server-local-timezone offsets, producing different slot times per deployment region with no error signal; the optional type hides the new mandatory-ness of the field for this code path.

[ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff covers the happy path of the getSlots offset math; none of the new checkIfIsAvailable branches (busy-vs-override bypass, working-hours rejection, boundary slots at override start/end, the `===` dead branch) are exercised by any test in the diff. A regression in the newly added bookability logic — e.g. the busy-check bypass on override days that permits double-booking — ships undetected, because the added assertion never places a booking on an override day or probes boundary times.

[BUG] The new working-hours rejection branch computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` check actually tests the slot's start minute. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after the closing time (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 5 minutes before close) is reported as available; bookings can be accepted that extend past the end of the user's working hours.

[BUG] The working-hours check uses `workingHours.find()` and returns 'unavailable' when ANY single workingHour entry does not contain the slot, which is the negation of the correct 'available only if inside SOME entry' semantics when a day has multiple ranges. A schedule with split shifts on one day (two workingHour entries for the same weekday, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00) rejects every slot on that day: a slot inside range A is rejected by range B and vice versa, so the user's availability silently disappears.

[BUG] `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits availability with true for any slot on a date-override day that falls inside an override window, skipping the `busy.every(...)` check entirely. Existing bookings that fall inside a date-override window no longer block slots, so the same time can be offered twice (double-booking) on override days.

[BUG] The override's local date is computed with the inverted offset (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` then added to `date.start`) and compared against the slot's raw UTC date (`slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`), so the override is matched against the wrong calendar day whenever the conversion crosses midnight. For an organizer at +6:00, an override stored as Jan 2 03:00Z (Jan 2 local) is shifted back to Jan 1 21:00 and compared to the slot's UTC date, so overrides near date boundaries match the wrong day and slots outside the override window (e.g. local 05:00 on the override day) are returned as available while legitimate override-day slots in adjacent UTC days are rejected.

[BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false, making this branch dead code. The intended zero-length-override fast path never fires; zero-length overrides fall through to the range checks and behave as an all-day block instead of the intended semantics.

[BUG] `dateOverrides` is flattened across ALL users and passed via `availabilityCheckProps` into every per-user `checkIfIsAvailable` call, while `organizerTimeZone` is the individual user's timezone, so one user's override makes every other user appear available on that day. For fixed-host/team schedules, a slot on a day where any single host has a date override is marked available for hosts who have no override that day (and the busy check is skipped for them), attributing slots to users who are not actually available.

[ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff exercises the lib/slots.ts override offset math with one happy-path scenario, and no assertion in the diff covers any of the new checkIfIsAvailable branches (slot-outside-override rejection, the dateOverrideExist short-circuit, or the working-hours rejection). The rewrite of checkIfIsAvailable — the highest-risk logic in this PR — ships with zero behavioral assertions; the mechanical defects above (end=start, `===` on dayjs objects, busy-check bypass) would all have been caught by tests exercising a slot partially overlapping an override window or a booking inside an override window, and any regression there passes CI silently.

[ADVISORY] The new test's expected slot list is byte-identical to the preceding assertion in the same block and its comment ('it should return the same as this is the utc time') asserts invariance, so if the fixture override's timeZone coincides with the requested +6:00 the new offset arithmetic is a no-op and the test also passes against the pre-change code. The test provides false confidence for the PR's headline change: it cannot detect an inverted offset direction or an off-by-offset shift because it contains no contrasting case (e.g. an override whose local calendar date differs from its UTC date) that would fail if the sign were wrong.

[ADVISORY] The new code unconditionally calls `.tz(override.timeZone)` although `TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, so an override without a timeZone falls back to the server's local timezone for the offset computation instead of a defined behavior. Any caller of getSlots that supplies date overrides without timeZone (the type explicitly permits it, and getSlots is an exported utility used outside this PR's call sites) gets environment-dependent slot results: the same request returns different availability depending on the server's TZ setting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `dateOverrides` are flattened across all users (`userAvailability.flatMap(...)`) and now include `timeZone` per override, but `checkIfIsAvailable` receives `dateOverrides` as a single array (not filtered by user) and does not reference `date.timeZone` at all. Instead it computes the day-match offset using only the passed `organizerTimeZone` (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`), while call sites pass `organizerTimeZone` as the current schedule/user timezone (`organizerTimeZone: schedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule?.timeZone`). Because the loop in `checkIfIsAvailable` iterates all overrides regardless of owner, an override belonging to another host will be evaluated using the wrong timezone offset and can incorrectly suppress/allow slots on the wrong UTC day. This is a correctness defect visible from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, once a date override exists for the slot’s day (`dateOverrideExist` set to true inside the `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback), the function returns `true` immediately (`if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`) before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` block. This means on any day with a date override, a slot that falls within the override window is considered available without checking `busy` times, allowing double-booking against existing calendar/booking conflicts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object references with `===`, which is always false, making the equal-start/end override branch dead code. Whatever behavior was intended for a zero-length date override (start equal to end) is never exercised: the branch silently never fires, so zero-length overrides fall through to the interval-overlap checks whose behavior for start==end was not the designed one.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the code `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separately constructed Dayjs instances by reference, so it will never be true. This makes the intended “start equals end” (zero-length override) branch effectively dead, and such overrides will instead fall through to the subsequent before/after interval logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new working-hours check compares `slotStartTime` (explicitly `.utc()`) day-of-week and UTC minutes-of-day directly against `workingHours.startTime/endTime` and `workingHour.days` without applying the utcOffset conversion the slot generator applies to the same workingHours structure. For an organizer whose schedule timezone is not UTC (e.g. UTC+6 with 09:00-17:00 local stored as 540-1020), a valid slot at 04:00 UTC (= 10:00 organizer local) has start=240 < 540 and is rejected, removing slots the generator produced as valid; the added test cannot catch this because its fixtures run in UTC where the frames coincide.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new “normal work hours” gate compares `slotStartTime` after forcing it to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc()`) against `workingHour.days` and `workingHour.startTime/endTime` using `slotStartTime.day()` and `slotStartTime.hour()*60+minute()` with no timezone conversion. If `workingHours` is defined in an organizer/schedule timezone (which is implied elsewhere in the diff by added `organizerTimeZone` and by timezone-offset adjustments for dateOverrides), this will incorrectly reject valid local-time slots whenever the organizer timezone is not UTC (day-of-week and minutes-of-day shift). The added test only exercises dateOverrides behavior and doesn’t cover working-hours timezone alignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] dateOverrides now carry a per-availability `timeZone` (the very field this PR adds to TimeRange), but checkIfIsAvailable ignores it and interprets every override against the single `organizerTimeZone` parameter. In ROUND_ROBIN/managed-team scheduling where hosts are in different timezones, a host's date override defined for a date in the host's local day resolves to a different calendar day in the organizer timezone and the day-match on line 117 fails, so the override is silently ignored and slots are computed from normal working hours on a day the host blocked.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `timeZone` onto each flattened `dateOverrides` entry (`availability.dateOverrides.map(... timeZone: availability.timeZone ...)`) and also adds `timeZone?: string` to `TimeRange`, but `checkIfIsAvailable` still computes its offset using only the single `organizerTimeZone` parameter (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset()`) and never reads `date.timeZone`. Therefore, any override intended to be interpreted in the host/availability timezone can be evaluated against a different timezone, making the day comparison (`format("YYYY MM DD")`) and boundary checks potentially wrong, which can cause overrides to be ignored/misapplied in multi-timezone setups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The offset math depends on `override.timeZone`, but packages/types/schedule.d.ts declares `timeZone?: string` as optional, so any producer of date overrides that does not set it gets `dayjs(...).tz(undefined)`, which resolves to the server's local timezone. Existing or third-party callers of getSlots that build overrides without the new field compile fine (the type is optional) and silently compute organizer/invitee offsets against the container's local timezone instead of the override's timezone, producing wrong slot times on any server not running in UTC; the optional type removes the compile-time guard that would force producers to update.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion logic unconditionally does `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` to compute `organizerUtcOffset`. However, the diff also updates `packages/types/schedule.d.ts` to make `timeZone?: string` optional on the override type. That means any existing caller that constructs date overrides without `timeZone` (still type-valid) will pass `undefined` into `.tz(...)`, and there is no fallback/guard in `getSlots` for that case. This can lead to incorrect offset math (or environment-dependent behavior) for overrides when `override.timeZone` is absent, exactly as the finding describes. The diff shows one producer (`getSchedule`) now sets `timeZone: availability.timeZone`, but it does not prove all producers do, and the optional type makes the mismatch silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The organizer and invitee UTC offsets are both computed at `override.start` and the single `offset` value is then applied to `override.end`, so an override window spanning a DST transition uses the wrong offset for its end. On dates where a DST shift occurs between the override's start and end (or between the override date and the invitee's slot date), the end time is shifted by one hour relative to the intended boundary, excluding or admitting slots along the override's closing edge on exactly the twice-a-year transition dates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new override conversion computes `organizerUtcOffset` and `inviteeUtcOffset` once using `override.start` (`dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(...).utcOffset()`), then applies the resulting single `offset` to both `override.start` and `override.end` (`dayjs(override.end).utc().add(offset, "minute")...`). If the override window spans a DST boundary (or if the relevant offset differs between the start and end instants), the end-time conversion will be off by the DST delta, shifting the computed `endTime` boundary and incorrectly including/excluding slots near the end edge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff's only test addition asserts one happy-path scenario (four slots present for a +6:00 invitee on the override day) and contains no assertion exercising any rejection branch of the new checkIfIsAvailable logic added in this same PR. The genuinely new behavior-bearing logic — slot-outside-override-window rejection on an override day, the working-hours boundary rejection (where the `end` bug and the UTC-frame mismatch above live), and the busy-bypass on override days — ships with zero coverage, so any regression in these branches, including the two bugs already present, passes CI undetected; a regression there re-opens already-booked or out-of-hours slots to booking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new branching logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (date-override existence tracking, “slot not within override” early `return false`, a working-hours “outside” early `return false`, and an override-day bypass that returns `true` before the existing busy checks). The only test added in `getSchedule.test.ts` asserts a single happy-path outcome (four slots returned for a +6:00 invitee) and does not assert any of the new rejection paths (e.g., slot outside override window on an override day, slot outside working hours when no override exists, or interactions with busy times). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in coverage for newly introduced behavior-bearing branches, not merely generic “add more tests.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The zero-length-override guard compares two dayjs objects with `===` (`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")`), which is reference equality on distinct objects and is always false. The intended early-return for a start===end date override never executes, so zero-length overrides fall through to the isBefore/isAfter comparisons and the branch's promised behavior is silently absent; the code ships as a no-op masked by its shape.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new zero-length override check uses `dayjs(...).add(...) === dayjs(...).add(...)` (reference equality). Since `dayjs()` creates new objects each call, this condition will never be true, so the intended special-case handling for `start === end` overrides cannot execute and the logic silently falls through to the other comparisons.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the new working-hours check, `end` is computed with the identical expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so `end > workingHour.endTime` tests the slot's start minute twice, never the slot's end. A slot that starts inside working hours but whose eventLength extends past `workingHour.endTime` (e.g. a 60-minute event starting at the last minute of the day) is accepted as available; bookings can be created for time the user does not work.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new working-hours guard computes both `start` and `end` from `slotStartTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so it never considers the slot’s actual end time (which depends on `eventLength`). As a result, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` cannot detect slots that start within working hours but extend past `workingHour.endTime`, matching the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] checkIfIsAvailable is expanded with a full working-hours enforcement block, which is work outside the PR's stated intent ('date override handling and timezone compatibility') and re-implements, inside the availability predicate, an invariant already enforced by slot generation (working hours gate which slots exist at all). Two parallel hand-maintained implementations of the working-hours rule now must agree; the duplication has already drifted (the broken start/end computation above), and the next change to working-hours semantics has to be made in two places or slot generation and booking-time validation silently diverge — users see bookable slots that the availability check later rejects or vice versa.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a working-hours enforcement block inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts). That block contains a concrete correctness defect: it computes both `start` and `end` identically from `slotStartTime` (`const start = ...; const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();`), so the end-of-slot check is wrong and can incorrectly mark slots as outside working hours. This is a real, diff-introduced behavioral bug. The finding’s broader point about duplicated working-hours logic is also supported by the presence of this new parallel check alongside existing slot-generation/working-hours logic in the codebase (e.g., working hours/overrides handling elsewhere), increasing divergence risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new offset math reads `override.timeZone`, which this same diff declares as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts line 5), and only the trpc getSchedule path was updated to populate it — any other producer of dateOverrides leaves it undefined, so `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(undefined)` resolves against the server's local timezone. On the un-updated call paths (the legacy apps/web getSchedule flow that consumes packages/lib getSlots), the organizer offset is taken from the server's host timezone: a deployment not running in UTC shifts every date override by the server offset and returns wrong slot times for date-override days; the fix's guarantee only holds on the one path the diff touched.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new offset logic calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` but `override.timeZone` is not guaranteed to exist: this diff explicitly makes it optional (`timeZone?: string` in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`). The only producer updated in this diff is the TRPC `getSchedule` mapping that adds `timeZone: availability.timeZone` to `dateOverrides`; any other construction of `activeOverrides`/`dateOverrides` would pass `timeZone` as `undefined`, and this code has no fallback (e.g., to `timeZone` or UTC). That can cause overrides to be interpreted using the runtime/server default timezone and shift slots incorrectly on non-UTC hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The router's date-override date matching applies the offset with inverted sign (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` added to the UTC instant), contradicting the convention used in packages/lib/slots.ts in the same diff (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset`, using the positive organizer offset); for an organizer in UTC+6 the override instant is shifted 6 hours backwards, moving it to the previous calendar day. For a non-UTC organizer, the override's shifted date no longer equals the slot's date, so `dateOverrideExist` stays false and the working-hours fallback (which has no availability on an override day) rejects the slot — date-override days produce no or wrong availability for non-UTC organizers. The added test does not catch this because its organizer timezone resolves to offset 0, making the `* -1` a no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), the override-day matching computes `utcOffset` as `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then *adds* it to `date.start`/`date.end` before comparing to `slotStartTime`’s UTC day. For a positive-offset organizer (e.g. UTC+6), this shifts the override instant 6 hours earlier (potentially into the previous UTC calendar day), which can prevent `dateOverrideExist` from being set and causes the function to fall back to the working-hours check. This sign/shift approach is inconsistent with the offset handling introduced in `packages/lib/slots.ts` (which derives a relative offset as `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and adds it), and the negative shift can plausibly misclassify override days for non-UTC organizers based purely on the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire new behavior-bearing logic in checkIfIsAvailable — date-override date matching, the dateOverrideExist shortcut, the working-hours fallback, and the organizerTimeZone plumbing — has no test in this diff; the only added test (apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts) exercises the separate legacy path through packages/lib/slots.ts getSlots. A regression in the date-override matching or working-hours filter (e.g. the sign or end-minute defects above) ships undetected: every booking-page availability query on the trpc path changes behavior with zero coverage, and the test that was added gives false assurance that 'timezone compatibility' was verified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts` inside `checkIfIsAvailable` (new `dateOverrides`/`workingHours` filtering, `dateOverrideExist` shortcut, and new `organizerTimeZone` plumbing). The only added test shown is in `apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts` and it does not reference the TRPC router file nor `checkIfIsAvailable`; meanwhile a separate change was made in `packages/lib/slots.ts` and the new test appears aligned with that scheduling/timezone slot-output behavior. From the diff alone, there is no added test coverage explicitly exercising the new `checkIfIsAvailable` logic, so regressions in that path could ship without coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A linear `userAvailability.find(...)` scan was added inside the per-slot, per-user availability filter on the schedule-generation hot path, executing once per user per slot candidate. Slot computation for event types with many fixed hosts and a wide date range now performs slots × users array scans where the previous code did a direct spread; for large round-robin teams this measurably lengthens every availability request, and the lookup result is loop-invariant per user yet recomputed per slot.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `userAvailability.find(...)` lookup inside the per-slot/per-user filtering loop: `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(({ user: { id: userId } }) => userId === slotUserId);` and then passes `organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone` to `checkIfIsAvailable` (see the block starting near `+ const userSchedule = ...` before `return checkIfIsAvailable`). This `find` runs once per `slotUserId` per slot candidate, making the hot path O(slots × users × userAvailability.length) instead of using a precomputed map. It’s a concrete performance/scalability concern introduced by the change, but not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, `end` is computed with the identical expression as `start` (`slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` comparison tests the slot's START against the working-hour end, never the slot's end. A slot that starts inside working hours but finishes after them (e.g. a 60-minute event starting on the last available minute) passes the `end > workingHour.endTime` test and is offered/bookable, producing bookings that extend beyond the host's availability; the check is also semantically dead weight since start and end are the same number.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` the new working-hours guard computes both `start` and `end` as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` (see `const start = ...; const end = ...;`). This makes `end` identical to `start`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` never checks the slot’s actual end (it should likely use `slotEndTime`). As a result, a slot whose start is within working hours but whose end exceeds `workingHour.endTime` will not be rejected by this check, allowing availability outside the host’s working hours.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` early-return reports a slot as available without ever running the `busy.every(...)` booking-overlap check that previously guarded every available verdict. On any day that has a date override, every slot falling inside the override window is returned as available even if the organizer already has a confirmed booking at that time, enabling double-booking on override days; the busy check is now skipped for exactly the slots this PR targets.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts), after computing `slotStartTime/slotEndTime`, the new logic sets `dateOverrideExist = true` when the slot’s day matches a `dateOverrides` entry, and if the `dateOverrides.find(...)` does not trigger the `return false` path, it immediately does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before reaching the final `return busy.every(...)` overlap check. This means slots that fall within a matching date override window can be marked available without considering existing `busy` bookings, enabling double-booking on override days.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false, so the equal-start/end short-circuit is dead code. A zero-length (start === end) date override never short-circuits; control falls through to the boundary checks, which then mark every slot NOT overlapping that instant as unavailable (slots ending before or starting after the instant return true from the find callback → slot rejected) while slots overlapping the zero-length instant bypass the busy check via dateOverrideExist — the exact inverse of any sane interpretation of an empty override.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the new logic compares two freshly-created Dayjs instances with `===`: `dayjs(date.start).add(... ) === dayjs(date.end).add(... )`. Since these are distinct objects, this condition is always false, making the intended “start equals end” short-circuit unreachable. This is a correctness defect directly present in the diff (object identity comparison instead of a value comparison like `.isSame()`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The date-override day match compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` (formatted in the server's LOCAL timezone, since dayjs defaults to local tz) against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where slotStartTime was explicitly forced to UTC via `time.utc()`. On any deployment whose server timezone is not UTC, the override's local-date string and the slot's UTC-date string are computed in two different calendars, so overrides match the wrong day (off by one near midnight boundaries) and override-day slots are silently dropped or wrongly kept; the behavior also becomes server-tz-dependent rather than deterministic.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, `slotStartTime` is forced to UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc()`), but the override-day match uses `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...)` where `dayjs(date.start)` defaults to the server's local timezone. This compares a locally-formatted calendar day to a UTC-formatted calendar day, making override matching dependent on server TZ and potentially off-by-one around midnight. The diff shows no `.utc()`/`.tz()` applied to the `dayjs(date.start)` used for formatting/comparison, so the finding is grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff silently repurposes checkIfIsAvailable from a pure busy/seat check into a full bookability check (working hours + date overrides), duplicating availability filtering that getSlots already performs with different math — a second source of truth introduced under a PR titled 'date override handling and timezone compatibility'. Every caller of checkIfIsAvailable gets changed verdicts even on non-override paths, and the two filters can disagree: getSlots shifts override wall-times by (invitee offset − organizer offset) while checkIfIsAvailable re-derives override dates from the organizer tz against UTC slot days, so a slot generated by getSlots can be rejected (or an out-of-window slot admitted) by the second filter; future changes to one path will silently break the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does expand `checkIfIsAvailable` from a busy/seats-only predicate into a broader bookability gate by adding `dateOverrides` + `workingHours` logic (new params at `checkIfIsAvailable` signature and the two early-return blocks). Separately, override/working-hours handling already exists in `packages/lib/slots.ts` via `activeOverrides` transforming working hours, with different timezone math (`offset = inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` and shifting override times). In contrast, `checkIfIsAvailable` re-derives override-day inclusion using `organizerTimeZone` and UTC slot-day comparisons (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1`, then comparing formatted YYYY MM DD). This introduces a second source of truth and makes it plausible for a slot emitted by the slot-generation path to be rejected (or vice versa) by the later filter, as the two computations are not the same. This is a specific, diff-grounded architecture/scope concern; the diff alone doesn’t prove a concrete failing case, but it clearly adds duplicated, potentially divergent filtering logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Three different notions of 'organizer timezone' now feed adjacent checks: the computed `organizerTimeZone` (eventType.timeZone || schedule.timeZone || userAvailability[0].timeZone) is passed to getSlots, while checkIfIsAvailable receives `schedule.timeZone`, `userSchedule.timeZone`, and `userSchedule?.timeZone` (which is undefined when no matching availability is found). A user whose availability row has no timeZone — or the `userSchedule?.timeZone` miss at the third call site — yields undefined, for which checkIfIsAvailable treats the UTC offset as 0 and matches override dates as if the organizer were in UTC; meanwhile getSlots used a possibly different tz, so slot generation and slot filtering disagree about which day an override covers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `checkIfIsAvailable` now depends on an optional `organizerTimeZone` to adjust date overrides (`organizerTimeZone ? dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() ... : 0`). But the callers pass three different values: a precomputed `organizerTimeZone` for `getSlots`, and for availability filtering they pass `schedule.timeZone`, `userSchedule.timeZone`, and `userSchedule?.timeZone` (which can be `undefined` if no matching availability is found). When `organizerTimeZone` is undefined, the override-day matching uses offset 0 (UTC), which can misclassify whether a slot is inside/outside an override day, while slot generation may have been based on a different timezone context. This creates a real correctness risk where slot generation and slot filtering disagree.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getSlots now unconditionally calls `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` while `TimeRange.timeZone` was added as optional (`timeZone?: string` in packages/types/schedule.d.ts), so any existing caller of getSlots that passes overrides without a timeZone gets `dayjs.tz(x, undefined)`, which resolves to the server's local timezone. Out-of-tree/internal callers of getSlots whose overrides carry no timeZone silently switch from the old getUTCHours behavior to server-local-timezone offsets, producing different slot times per deployment region with no error signal; the optional type hides the new mandatory-ness of the field for this code path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the override mapping now unconditionally does `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and similarly for `override.end`, with no fallback when `override.timeZone` is missing. Yet the diff also changes `TimeRange` to have `timeZone?: string` (optional) in `packages/types/schedule.d.ts`, meaning overrides can legally omit it. If `override.timeZone` is `undefined`, `dayjs.tz(..., undefined)` will not use the previous UTC-based `getUTCHours()` logic and can instead resolve using a default timezone (often server-local), producing deployment-dependent slot calculations with no error. While `getSchedule` now populates `timeZone` when flattening `dateOverrides`, other callers passing overrides without `timeZone` would be affected by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test added in this diff covers the happy path of the getSlots offset math; none of the new checkIfIsAvailable branches (busy-vs-override bypass, working-hours rejection, boundary slots at override start/end, the `===` dead branch) are exercised by any test in the diff. A regression in the newly added bookability logic — e.g. the busy-check bypass on override days that permits double-booking — ships undetected, because the added assertion never places a booking on an override day or probes boundary times.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new branching logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` (date override short-circuiting via `dateOverrideExist`, early `return false` when a slot is outside an override day, and a separate working-hours rejection path using `workingHours.find(...)`). The only new test added (`scheduleForEventOnADayWithDateOverrideDifferentTimezone`) asserts returned slot times for a timezone-offset scenario, but it does not introduce any `busy` booking on an override day, does not probe boundary conditions at override start/end, and does not exercise the working-hours rejection branch. Thus, the finding that the new bookability branches are not covered by added tests is grounded in the diff and is a concrete coverage gap rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new working-hours rejection branch computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime` (`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` duplicates the `start` expression), so the `end > workingHour.endTime` check actually tests the slot's start minute. A slot that starts inside working hours but ends after the closing time (e.g. a 60-minute slot starting 5 minutes before close) is reported as available; bookings can be accepted that extend past the end of the user's working hours.

[BUG] The working-hours check uses `workingHours.find()` and returns 'unavailable' when ANY single workingHour entry does not contain the slot, which is the negation of the correct 'available only if inside SOME entry' semantics when a day has multiple ranges. A schedule with split shifts on one day (two workingHour entries for the same weekday, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00) rejects every slot on that day: a slot inside range A is rejected by range B and vice versa, so the user's availability silently disappears.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the working-hours gate is implemented as `workingHours.find(...)` returning `true` when the slot is outside a given `workingHour` for that weekday, and then immediately returning `false` (unavailable) if any such entry is found. With multiple working-hour ranges on the same day, a slot that is inside range A will still be outside range B, causing `find` to match and the slot to be rejected. This matches the finding’s “split shifts reject everything” scenario and is grounded in the added code in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits availability with true for any slot on a date-override day that falls inside an override window, skipping the `busy.every(...)` check entirely. Existing bookings that fall inside a date-override window no longer block slots, so the same time can be offered twice (double-booking) on override days.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the new date-override logic runs, the function does `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }` before the final `return busy.every(...)` block. This means that for any slot on a day where a matching `dateOverrides` entry exists (and the earlier `find(...)` didn’t trigger the `return false` “outside override” case), availability is forced to `true` and the busy-time overlap checks are skipped entirely. From the diff alone, this would allow slots to be offered even if `busy` contains an overlapping booking on that override day/window (i.e., potential double-booking).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The override's local date is computed with the inverted offset (`dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` then added to `date.start`) and compared against the slot's raw UTC date (`slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")`), so the override is matched against the wrong calendar day whenever the conversion crosses midnight. For an organizer at +6:00, an override stored as Jan 2 03:00Z (Jan 2 local) is shifted back to Jan 1 21:00 and compared to the slot's UTC date, so overrides near date boundaries match the wrong day and slots outside the override window (e.g. local 05:00 on the override day) are returned as available while legitimate override-day slots in adjacent UTC days are rejected.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the override day match shifts `date.start` by `dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1` and then compares `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` against `slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD")` where `slotStartTime` is explicitly UTC (`time.utc()`). For a positive offset timezone (e.g. +6:00), multiplying by `-1` and adding moves the override timestamp backwards, which can cross midnight and cause the override to be associated with the wrong calendar day relative to the UTC slot date. This is directly grounded in the diff and would misclassify slots near date boundaries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct dayjs object instances with `===`, which is always false, making this branch dead code. The intended zero-length-override fast path never fires; zero-length overrides fall through to the range checks and behave as an all-day block instead of the intended semantics.

adjudication.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the code `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two newly-created Dayjs object instances by reference, which will never be `true`. That makes the “start == end” special-case branch effectively dead code. If the intent was to detect zero-length overrides, it should use `.isSame(...)` (or compare timestamps). This defect is directly visible in the diff and affects the override logic’s behavior for `start === end` cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `dateOverrides` is flattened across ALL users and passed via `availabilityCheckProps` into every per-user `checkIfIsAvailable` call, while `organizerTimeZone` is the individual user's timezone, so one user's override makes every other user appear available on that day. For fixed-host/team schedules, a slot on a day where any single host has a date override is marked available for hosts who have no override that day (and the busy check is skipped for them), attributing slots to users who are not actually available.

adjudication.rationale: In `getSchedule`, `dateOverrides` is flattened across all `userAvailability` (`flatMap`) and passed via `availabilityCheckProps` into `checkIfIsAvailable` for per-user checks, but `checkIfIsAvailable` never filters overrides by `userId`. Instead it scans all `dateOverrides` and, if any override matches the slot’s day, it sets `dateOverrideExist` and then returns `true` immediately (skipping working-hours and `busy` checks). Because `organizerTimeZone` is passed per-user (`schedule.timeZone` / `userSchedule.timeZone`), one user’s override can affect availability decisions for other users, making them appear available on that day even without their own override.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new code unconditionally calls `.tz(override.timeZone)` although `TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional in packages/types/schedule.d.ts, so an override without a timeZone falls back to the server's local timezone for the offset computation instead of a defined behavior. adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/slots.ts the new logic computes offsets with `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()`.
